speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing a psychiatric condition along with new-onset movement issues; to help me understand your situation, could you please describe the specific movements you are seeing and when they started?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is helpful; since the risperidone was started two months ago, has the movement disorder been constant or is it intermittent? Also, have you noticed any stiffness, tremors, or difficulty moving your limbs?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming the labs are normal. Given your diagnosis of schizophrenia and recent risperidone use, are these movements involuntary (like tremors or muscle spasms) or do they resemble a "shaking of the head" or facial grimacing? Also, have you noticed any stiffness, slowness of movement, or a feeling that something is "stuck" in your throat?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for describing those sensations; they sound like akathisia, a common side effect of the risperidone you are taking. To confirm this and rule out other causes, have you noticed any worsening of your restlessness after taking your morning dose, and does taking a small amount of caffeine make it worse?

REQUEST TEST: Risperidone_Serum_Level
REQUEST IMAGES: Neurological_Examination_Notes

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on your symptoms of restlessness, fidgeting, and inability to remain still after starting risperidone, this is highly suggestive of drug-induced akathisia. Before we finalize the plan, I need to know if you have noticed any new muscle stiffness or jaw clenching that might indicate a different side effect.

REQUEST TEST: Prolactin_Level

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal prolactin level makes Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome and severe hyperprolactinemia less likely, which aligns with your description of subjective restlessness and motor fidgeting. To confirm the diagnosis of drug-induced akathisia, I need to know if this inner sense of restlessness has significantly worsened your quality of life or if you have ever felt compelled to keep moving to relieve the discomfort.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-Induced Akathisia
